articles.title: Singapore GP: George Russell tops sole practice from Charles Leclerc ahead of Sprint Qualifying
articles.summary: George Russell will start at the back for Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix but came out of the blocks flying by topping Practice; watch Sprint Qualifying later on Friday at 1.30pm ahead of the Singapore Sprint itself on Saturday at 10am, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Russell, who will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change, was 0.198s quicker than Ferrari's Leclerc as Mercedes look to bounce back from their "worst weekend of the season" in Malaysia, according to team boss Toto Wolff.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was over one second off the pace in seventh but did not run the soft tyres and made a mistake at the end of practice.

Mercedes have decided to revert to the pre-Malaysia car with Russell, so he does not carry the big upgrade package from last time out while Antonelli has kept the new parts, plus a new front wing.

The hot, dusty conditions make practice largely unrepresentative but it will be fascinating to see if Russell has the upper hand on pace over Antonelli in Sprint Qualifying on Friday afternoon at 1.30pm (build-up from 1pm), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event .

McLaren's Lando Norris has scored just two points from the last two race weekends, partly due to a straight-line speed issue which McLaren think they have resolved, and he appears to be back in the fight at the front at just 0.273s adrift of pacesetter Russell.

Lewis Hamilton was half a second behind in fourth on a track Ferrari should be competitive at due to the lack of straights at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri in fifth.

Last week's race winner Max Verstappen was only sixth but Red Bull elected to not run the softs and the Dutchman was the fastest driver on the mediums.

Singapore is the only track, apart from Madrid which joined the calendar this year, which Verstappen has not taken a pole position or win at in his F1 career.

Isack Hadjar was eighth in the other Red Bull while Alpine and Racing Bulls look set to continue their fight for the final points-paying positions with Pierre Gasly in ninth and Liam Lawson in 10th.

Despite the close proximity of the barriers, there were few incidents aside from Audi's Nico Hulkenberg losing drive and causing a brief Virtual Safety Car when he stopped at the pit exit.

articles.title: El WRC 2027, con tres novedades y Canarias presente
articles.standfirst: Desaparece un clásico como Portugal, pero entran tres nuevas localizaciones de cara al año de los cambios
articles.summary: Desaparece un clásico como Portugal, pero entran tres nuevas localizaciones de cara al año de los cambios
articles.body: Tras la épica resolución del 2026, el título de Evans y la cuenta atrás a la nueva era del 2027, el Mundial de Rallyes (WRC) ha completado otro paso indispensable previo a la acción, el presentar su calendario del nuevo curso. Algo más tarde que otros campeonatos FIA, con 15 citas, tres novedades y la presencia del Rally Islas Canarias como la prueba española presente en el calendario tras su entrada en 2025 tras los muchos cursos del Cataluña dentro de la máxima categoría. El Islas Canarias, disputado en la isla de Gran Canaria, se ha ganado a pulso estar dentro del Mundial. Sus tramos, su gente y el espectáculo vivido lo ha convertido en una prueba obligatoria que tendrá lugar entre el 6 y el 9 de mayo. Será la segunda de asfalto de las cuatro en la primera parte de la temporada antes de otra decisión en citas de tierra y grava. Lo habitual en tiempos modernos, con los campeonatos ganándose en el polvo y el juego entre órdenes de salida. El Mundial, más allá del sabor español, empezará en Montecarlo (21 al 24 de enero), cerrará en Arabia Saudí (25 al 28 de noviembre) -si no ocurre nada raro- y cuenta con tres puntos importantes en las citas que se estrenan. Por supuesto, siguen presentes los clásicos del Mundial como la nieve de Suecia, el durísimo Acrópolis de Grecia o la velocidad alta de Finlandia. Además del exotismo del asfalto de Japón o la dureza de la doble cita sudamericana en Paraguay y Chile al final de campaña. La que no estará es Portugal, principal ausencia. En el terreno de las novedades, la primera será Italia (8 al 11 de julio), que abandona Cerdeña y realizará una cita de asfalto con Roma como el lugar que encabeza las quinielas. En el tramo final de campaña vendrán las otras dos, con la novedad de los Estados Unidos (26 al 29 de agosto) y el regreso de una cita en las Islas Británicas. En este caso, Escocia es la nación elegida entre el 30 de septiembre y el 3 de octubre. En total, 15 rallyes, el mayor número desde 2008, y un nuevo Mundial en el que el reglamento 2027 entrará en acción para buscar al nuevo rey del campeonato. Evans ya sabe dónde tendrá que defender la corona más épica que se recuerda en la era moderna del WRC. En un par de meses arranca la acción real.

articles.summary: Vamos a ir cerrando por aquí... pero no sin antes recordaros que mañana tenemos Sprint y Clasificación. Lo primero... la Sprint será a las 11.00 y la
articles.body:
Última hora de la Clasificación Sprint F1, en directo

Vuelven las Sprint a la F1 . Estamos en Marina Bay , con el Gran Premio de Singapur y tras los Entrenamientos Libres 1 comienza la acción con la Clasificación al Sprint .

Esta mañana Russell se ha llevado el mejor crono con un 1.32.274 , seguido de Charles Leclerc , quien se ha quedado a 198 milésimas y del piloto de McLaren , Lando Norris, a quien le ha sacado un total de 273 milésimas .

Un Entrenamiento Libre que comenzó con unanimidad (prácticamente) en la elección del compuesto más duro , pero que poco a poco fue siendo más variopinto al ir montando tanto los neumáticos medios como los blandos.

Mientras, el líder del Mundial, Kimi Antonelli, finalizó la primera sesión en 7º lugar a 1.251 de su compañero de equipo, Russell, aunque en diversas ocasiones llegara a liderar la tabla de tiempos.

El último ganador de Gran Premio, Max Verstappen , finalizó la sesión 6º , a 732 milésimas, apretando aún más los tiempos y metiendo así más variedad de marcas en lo alto de la clasificación. Aunque todo el mundo espera que sean los Mercedes los que acaben dominando, este tipo de situaciones donde se ve claramente a algún Ferrari, McLaren o Red Bull al frente, nos da las esperanzas de que no haya un solo dominador y que la lucha se pueda abrir un poco más.

Por último, aunque no por ello menos importante, los españoles. Ambos pilotos tuvieron un entrenamiento de adaptación en el que no llegaron a montar el compuesto más blando, quedando Alonso , 14º y Sainz , 15º a poco menos de segundo y medio de George Russell . No obstante, y a pesar del resultado final, tanto en Aston Martin como en Williams , a pesar de las dificultades, no pierden la esperanza de que sus pilotos vuelva a tirar de talento y darles una buena posición para mañana la Sprint .

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Desert Castle can continue winning sequence in the Dewhurst
articles.summary: Despite still recovering from injury, Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle will have a keen eye on Newmarket as the Dewhurst looms this weekend; Speaking to Simon Mapletoft, Hollie took time to preview the pick of some top-class action from Headquarters and the Knavesmire.
articles.body:
Castle to give Appleby his fourth Dewhurst

Charlie Appleby can enhance his great record in the Group One Darley Dewhurst Stakes (3.00) at Newmarket on Saturday with the unbeaten Desert Castle .

Godolphin's trainer has won it three times in the last seven years, most recently with Shadow Of Light in 2024, and has no qualms about pitching his exciting son of Frankel into the highest company for the first time.

He impressed me with his dominance in the Group Two Champagne Stakes at Doncaster last month - his first outing since stepping out of novice company - and can cement his place at the head of the 2,000 Guineas market.

Aidan O'Brien's Ante-post Derby favourite Darkness Falls has already won at this level so poses a considerable threat, but I'm not convinced the drop back to seven-furlongs will be in his favour.

Mountain to climb to prominence in Cesarewitch

Brian Ellison's Sea Lantern could be very well treated in the Club Godolphin Cesarewitch Handicap (3.40) at Newmarket, but I prefer another northern raider in the stayers' showpiece.

Mountain Road was a solid second to the strongly fancied Small Fry over two-miles at York and should appreciate the extra quarter-mile with Paul Mulrennan back on board for the first time since his win at Thirsk in the summer.

Sea Lantern could be anything at this stage and Brian has made no secret of how highly he rates the ex-Irish gelding, who has won at Pontefract since chasing home the smart duo Infraad and Asia Force at the West Yorkshire track.

This represents a considerable step up in grade and trip for the son of Sea The Stars but he looks a thorough stayer who may be underestimated by his mark of 89, which includes a four-pound penalty.

The Lost King is a worthy favourite for the Group Three Modern Games Darley Stakes (1.15) at Newmarket on the evidence of his second in the Joel Stakes over a mile last time.

The way he finished behind the classy Talk Of New York in a higher grade that day suggests he should enjoy the extra furlong in pursuit of more Pattern success for his trainer Andrew Balding.

Haatem has been on his travels, winning a Grade Three at Kentucky Downs, and Wathnan Racing's ultra-tough five-year-old will be a huge threat to all his rivals with Ryan Moore on board if he's on his A-game.

Drumbeat sets standard in Zetland Stakes

It will be interesting to see how Drumbeat copes with the step up in trip in the Group Three Native Trail Zetland Stakes (1.50) at Newmarket.

Aidan O'Brien's colt sets the standard with that third in the Group Two Beresford Stakes at The Curragh last time and despite being out of a sprint mare gives the impression he will appreciate this extra quarter-mile.

Though he needs to improve markedly, Andrew Balding's Wykehurst Park looks interesting at bigger odds. This son of Stradivarius has only won a Yarmouth maiden, but Andrew wouldn't be running him if he didn't think he was Pattern class.

Aidan O'Brien's Sergei Diaghilev was unlucky to bump into Dewhurst favourite Desert Castle in the Champagne Stakes at Doncaster last time, but compensation awaits in the Group Three Emirates Autumn Stakes (2.25) at Newmarket.

He's a smart colt, having beaten Group One winner Folsom Blues on debut before taking a Listed race in Ireland, and can put his experience to good use.

By contrast, Rock Montreal has only had two starts including a second in the Listed Flying Scotsman Stakes at Doncaster's St Leger Festival while Sole Ambition's form has been franked since winning a maiden at this track last month and is another who can step forward.

Agamemnon puts down a solid marker for the Sky Bet Rockingham Stakes (1.30) at York on Saturday with his fourth in the Group Two Gimcrack Stakes over the same course and distance in August.

He couldn't build on that back over the minimum trip in the Flying Childers, but Richard Hughes' Group-placed son of Mehmas looks to have been found a winning opportunity at Listed level.

I've always liked Richard Hannon's Cut A Dash who has found life tough since finishing fourth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot but won on his debut at this track and should appreciate a return to calmer waters.

My husband Tom Marquand has an outstanding chance in the Sky Bet Sprint Trophy Handicap (3.17) at York on Saturday with the talented Binhareer .

William Haggas' course and distance winner didn't see much daylight in bottomless ground in the Ayr Gold Cup but should have conditions much more to his liking on The Knavesmire.

Mick Appleby's likely favourite Coul Angel bolted up in a hot race at The Curragh last month and must go well but has to defy an eight-pound rise in a red-hot sprint handicap.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft .

articles.title: Super Sprint tips: Kate, Sam and Dec make three different cases for Chepstow feature
articles.summary: The panel of Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Declan Rix paid special attention to Chepstow’s feature Handicap Hurdle, the Silver Trophy
articles.body:
Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies will be hoping that Masked Man can win at this fixture for the second year in a row as he heads the market for another ultra-competitive renewal of the Silver Trophy at Chepstow.

"I'm siding with the Double Green-owned machine that is Masked Man for Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies. He won at this meeting last year making his first run under rules, he was competitive in all of them starts last season and they even chanced him in the Grade One at Aintree.

"His trainer combination are flying at the minute, with a 50 per cent strike rate and I know he is favourite, but he is still a good price and will be ready to go for this."

"I went to Olly Murphy's last week for a stable tour and the first horse and the one he kept mentioning was Daylatedollarshort with Sean Bowen on. He showed progression in handicaps after being a little bit disappointing in his career.

"He ran an almighty race at the Punchestown Festival when finishing second. He looked fit and ready to go last week, and he could land the race for the same connections that won this race last year."

" Washington is a huge price here. He may be a 10-year-old, but this is his time of year. He loves racing in Wales in October and his record in this month is where he is at his peak.

"He could go well at a massive price for a trainer in Harry Derham, who hasn't been in the winner's enclosure for a while but has provided plenty of placed efforts from his runners so far. He's a good each-way bet at a huge price."

articles.title: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says people who think team favour Kimi Antonelli over George Russell are 'brainless' and should 'watch Teletubbies'
articles.summary: Toto Wolff has dismissed suggestions Mercedes have favoured championship leader Kimi Antonelli over his team-mate George Russell; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
articles.body:
Antonelli has defied pre-season expectations to build an 84-point lead over Russell at the top of the Drivers' Championship with just seven races remaining, including this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

Wolff offered a scathing response to the suggestion Mercedes do not treat their drivers equally, which included a reference to criticism the team previously faced from Lewis Hamilton fans before the seven-time world champion left to join Ferrari.

"They're brainless, whoever thinks that," Wolff said on Friday in Singapore.

"It's completely nonsensical. We've had it in the past with Lewis fans."

Russell will start from the back of the grid in Singapore after an engine failure last weekend in Malaysia forced him into taking a penalty.

The Brit also confirmed on Thursday that he is likely to have to incur a further grid penalty before the end of the season given the position he has been left in by multiple technical failures.

Antonelli has also suffered from poor reliability this season, with technical issues costing the 20-year-old significant points hauls in Barcelona and at Silverstone.

Despite the problems, Mercedes are closing in on a first constructors' title since 2021, as they hold a 151-point lead over Ferrari at the top of the standings.

Wolff continued: "I don't know what's going on. Do they think I have a button that says, 'George, engine failure now?'

"Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we're fighting for the Constructors' Championship, when we've always had the mindset of providing everybody with equal material."

The Austrian suggested the situation is potentially a product of the way social media is used, but insisted that he is ultimately amused by it.

"I guess this is maybe where social media goes today," he added. "People hide behind their screens and then they lash out. There's a lot of polarisation going on.

"Sometimes I read what people write, I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they're abusing the team or myself. I'm Satan, I've heard. Overall, funny.

"Zero understanding and respect for people who come up with these things. Rather than watching Formula 1, they should do Teletubbies, or some Mickey Mouses."

'I feel a lot of emotions and compassion for George'

Wolff offered a further response to the idea that he favours Antonelli by revealing elements of the close relationship he and his wife Susie Wolff share with Russell and the Brit's partner Carmen Montero Mundt.

He said: "We have had Kimi since he was 11. He's integral part of the team. It's very nice to see him grow, be in a position now that he's fighting for a championship at such a young age, the talent he has.

"On the other side, George, who's been with us since he was 17. Someone that I feel a lot of, how can I say, emotions for and compassion.

"We are very close. We spend time with Carmen and Susie off the track with each other. If people would see that we're traveling together, we're having coffee in the same coffee shop, we're going in a gym.

"That's why it's pretty annoying to have some lunatics that have no understanding really about how relationships work coming up with these kind of accusations. I don't pay any attention to this.

articles.title: Un golpe de Checo afecta a Sainz y mete en problemas a Verstappen
articles.standfirst: El español saldrá último -22º- en el sprint (11 horas, DAZN) tras un viernes que se complicó en el momento más importante
articles.summary: El español saldrá último -22º- en el sprint (11 horas, DAZN) tras un viernes que se complicó en el momento más importante
articles.body: Sólo había un libre en el Gran Premio de Singapur y todo lo demás iba a ser batalla real. Es algo diferente, difícil y que afectó a la Fórmula 1 desde el pistoletazo de salida de la clasificación sprint en Marina Bay. Uno de los implicados más destacados fue Carlos Sainz, enviándole al fondo de la parrilla de la carrera corta del sábado (11 horas, DAZN), y puede golpear las opciones de uno de los máximos favoritos, el neerlandés Max Verstappen. Se espera ruido hasta un tiempo después de la sesión... En la SQ1 se originó el lío mucho antes de los primeros giros buenos. Sergio Pérez contactó con el muro poco antes de los primeros cuatro minutos de sesión, siguió en marcha y la situación peligrosa, con la pieza en pista, provocó la bandera roja. Que dejó a los pilotos con menos tiempo y provocó, al mismo tiempo, un jaleo entre Max Verstappen y Lewis Hamilton. El neerlandés adelantó con la bandera amarilla a su rival acérrimo y los comisarios comenzaron de inmediato la investigación. "Me ha adelantado con bandera amarilla", se quejaba el de Ferrari. Mientras tanto, su histórico rival sólo podía poner excusas que suenan a demasiado poco si los comisarios aplican un criterio habitual en su decisión. "Le dejé pasar porque la situación era complicada, creo que le adelanté antes de la bandera amarilla. Pero quiero comprobarlo", reportaba Verstappen. Su fuerza tras ganar en Malasia puede recibir un revés en una pista donde jamás ha ganado. El que ganó en Singapur y siempre lucha en la pista asiática es Carlos Sainz. Pero el sprint se antoja difícil, pues tendrá que partir desde el fondo de la parrilla de salida. Cayó en la SQ1 con sólo un intento tras el golpe de Pérez y no tuvo la capacidad de mejorar en una vuelta que venía condenada desde los primeros momentos. Su apuesta vendrá en el formato clásico, aunque no parece sencillo. "Tengo mucho bloqueo delantero y no noto la trasera. Se combina", explicaba el madrileño a través de la radio. Su error fundamental vino en la curva 8, donde no pudo colocar el coche en una curva muy ancha. Se quedó lejos del pase, perdió más de tres segundos y su posición empeoró tras terminar la sesión pues se encontró un error en el cronometraje que provocó que, por ejemplo, Bortoleto pasase el corte y el 55 cayese al fondo de la tabla.

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix: Mercedes F1 boss Toto Wolff's anger at bias claims
articles.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 boss Toto Wolff rejects accusations of team of bias against George Russell, calling critics "brainless".
articles.body:
Mercedes Formula 1 boss Toto Wolff says critics who accuse the team of bias against George Russell are "brainless".

The British driver's championship hopes were all but extinguished by an engine failure while he was running third at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday.

Russell enters this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix 86 points behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, and will start from the back because of a grid penalty for using too many engine parts.

Wolff described accusations of favouritism towards Antonelli as "completely nonsensical".

He added: "We've had it in the past with Lewis (Hamilton) fans.

"I mean, literally, I don't know what's going on. Do they think I have a button that says, 'George engine failure now', or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we are fighting for a Constructors' Championship, when we have always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material?

"But I guess this is maybe where social media goes today. People hide behind their screens and then they lash out.

"There's a lot of polarisation going on, and sometimes I read what people write. I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they are abusing the team or myself. I'm Satan, I've heard."

Wolff emphasised that he had always pursued a policy of equality between drivers since he took over the leadership of Mercedes in 2013.

He underlined his close personal relationship with Russell and Antonelli, who are both long-time proteges of the team and Wolff personally.

"We have had Kimi since he was 11," Wolff said. "He is an integral part of the team.

"It is very nice to see him grow, be in a position now that he is fighting for a championship at such a young age, the talent he has.

"And then on the other side, George, who has been with us since he was 17, someone that I feel a lot of, how can I say, emotions for and compassion. We are very close."

He said he and his wife Susie socialise with Russell and his fiancee Carmen Montero Mundt.

"We are spending time with Carmen and Susie off the track with each other," he said. "If people would see that we're travelling together, we're having coffee in the same coffee shop, we're going to the gym.

"That's why it's pretty annoying to have some lunatics that have no understanding really about how relationships work coming up with these kinds of accusations.

"So, I don't pay any attention to this. Most important is that George knows how the team is and Kimi knows, and we will always try to give them equal opportunity."

He said a "good example" of the equal treatment of both drivers was this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

The team has decided to split the specification of its cars at Marina Bay after an upgrade in Malaysia last weekend failed to provide the expected step forward in performance.

Russell is using the previous spec car and Antonelli the new one.

Wolff said: "We don't know which one is going to be quicker."

He said initial indications were that the "new car seems to be a little more tricky to drive - not saying it's necessarily slower, because there will be goodness in it, but maybe we haven't just found a way of putting it all together and tuning it.

"The older car is a bit more stable, grippy, but that is really just one data point. That is one free practice session, and it will be needing more time to really come to more conclusive information."

He said the success or otherwise of the upgrade, Mercedes' first significant change to the car's design since June, could have significant ramifications on Mercedes' preparations for 2027.

"We've put a few months of upgrades into the car, clearly pointing in a direction that we think is advantageous," Wolff said, "and maybe we just need to calibrate it a little bit in order to find the right way forward for 2027."

articles.title: Daryz retired: Francis-Henri Graffard's dual Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe hero heads to stud for owners Aga Khan
articles.summary: Daryz became the first colt since 1978 to win back-to-back Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe titles last Sunday; owned by the Aga Khan Studs, he will now start his new career as a sire; Christophe Soumillon in to ride Calandagan on Champions Day at Ascot
articles.body:
Francis-Henri Graffard's four-year-old became the first colt since Alleged in 1977 and 1978 to land back-to-back renewals of Europe's premier middle-distance contest, while he is the ninth dual winner overall.

No horse has ever won the Arc three times, but Daryz will not be bidding for the hat-trick in 12 months' time, with a second career in the breeding shed awaiting him next year.

In all Daryz won nine of his 12 career starts, earning almost £5.5million in prize-money. He won four Group Ones, having earlier this season claimed the Prix Ganay and the Prix Aga Khan IV at his beloved ParisLongchamp to go with his two Arc triumphs.

A statement from the Aga Khan Studs read: "Daryz, the brilliant dual Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner, has been retired from racing following his historic second victory in Europe's premier contest on Sunday at ParisLongchamp.

"Renowned for his exceptional turn of foot, Daryz echoed his own sire Sea The Stars by combining class with the versatility to excel over a range of distances and ground conditions. He retires as a six-time Group winner, including four victories at Group One level from nine to 12 furlongs."

The statement added: "Daryz now embarks on a new chapter in his story as part of the Aga Khan Studs stallion roster. Further details regarding stud arrangements will be announced in due course."

The Aga Khan team also confirmed that with Mickael Barzalona sidelined by suspension for Champions Day at Ascot on Saturday week, Christophe Soumillon will partner globetrotting star Calandagan in his defence of the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes, while the Belgian will also be on board Rayif in the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes.

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix: Max Verstappen beats George Russell to Singapore sprint pole
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen beats Mercedes driver George Russell to sprint pole at the Singapore Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen beat Mercedes driver George Russell to sprint pole at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Verstappen, fresh from his and Red Bull's first victory of the season in Malaysia last weekend, was 0.12 seconds quicker than the Briton, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc third.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were fourth and fifth ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who went early in final qualifying and fell down the order from initially being second behind Leclerc.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli, using the Mercedes upgrade that underperformed in Malaysia while Russell is on the previous specification, could manage only seventh.

And there were further glitches with the engine settings provided by governing body the FIA five days after the formation laps in the wet in Malaysia saw cars reduced to crawling speed as a result of a software bug.

Mercedes critics think I'm Satan - Wolff

The settings issue in Singapore, which was combined with a glitch in the F1 timing system that delayed the start of second qualifying, affected all cars but had a bigger impact on some drivers than others, depending on the timing of their runs.

The problem involved the settings being different before and after a red flag caused by a crash for Sergio Perez's Cadillac and left drivers complaining of reduced power.

It involved overtake mode - which allows an extra 0.5MJ of energy to be harvested - being switched on and off again in the space of 28 seconds.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz was knocked out in the first session after what we described as a "really poor lap", but added: "On top of that, half the cars did the lap with half a second quicker engine than the others.

"There was another software issue and we were on the bad end of it, and for whatever reason, the FIA, like in Malaysia, again didn't decide to do sporting equity and were happy to do half of the quali with cars with higher power than the other half of the cars.

"A bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things depending on who is out in Q1 or who is out in lap one."

Sainz said he did not think he would have made it through even without the settings problem.

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll were other drivers who were affected and were knocked out in the first session. Stroll's team-mate Fernando Alonso also suffered, but did progress, eventually qualifying 15th.

The FIA said in a statement: "During the first period of sprint qualifying there was a human error in race control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1.

"This issue in question meant overtake mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1.

"When it became apparent that overtake mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap.

"The second and third periods of sprint qualifying were not affected."

The FIA system automatically disables overtake mode when there is a red flag. A pop-up then appears on the screen asking whether officials want to re-enable it.

This was ignored, then overtake mode was reactivated before being disabled again, on the basis that it was fairer to do so than leave it enabled.

Upgraded Mercedes 'very difficult, very unpredictable'

Verstappen's pole lap appeared to be further confirmation of Red Bull's resurgence after his dominant win in Malaysia.

He faced an investigation for overtaking Hamilton under yellow flags shown before the first session was stopped for the Perez incident, but officials took no further action.

The four-time champion said he had not believed pole was possible before qualifying.

"We have some difficulties with the car in ride, as we know," he said, "but at least when we went to the soft tyres (in the final session), it made the car a bit more stable in places where before you were a bit unsure.

"I did not expect this but you take it, I'm happy for sure. Qualifying tomorrow is still the main goal and for us the start is always a critical point but at least a positive end to our day."

Russell's performance compared with that of Antonelli raises further doubts about the efficacy of the Mercedes upgrade introduced in Malaysia.

It was their biggest car update since the Canadian Grand Prix in May but team boss Toto Wolff said at Sepang that it had appeared to take them backwards rather than forwards.

Mercedes split the car spec here in Singapore in an attempt to better understand its performance but Antonelli ended the session 0.573secs behind Russell.

The Briton said: "As a team there is still nothing telling us it isn't working but it's all driven by the stopwatch and, yeah, the stopwatch hasn't been great for the upgrade yet. Maybe tomorrow's a different day."

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Antonelli, who leads the championship by 84 points going into the weekend, said: "Already FP1 I was struggling and there is still a lot to understand about this package. Really the car is very difficult, very unpredictable, very difficult to put a lap together. It's a shame. I was coming with high hopes but so far it has been very difficult.

"It's going to be a difficult weekend unless we can pull something out tomorrow. Other than that it is going very tricky. I don't really see where we can find 0.7secs but you never know."

Wolff said before sprint qualifying: "The new car seems to be a little more tricky to drive. Not saying it's necessarily slower, because there will be goodness in it, but maybe we haven't just found a way of putting it all together and tuning it. The older car is a bit more stable, grippy, but that is really just one data point."

Leclerc was 0.243secs off pole, and ruing what he said was Ferrari "losing a little bit of our raw performance" in the past three or four races.

However, he added: "Still I feel there is potential in the car and maybe tomorrow we can be there or thereabouts in fighting for pole."

Hamilton said: "We did a slightly different run plan to the others. It was my choice, but I think we got that wrong. But ultimately, the car was very oversteery on that lap. If the rears [tyres] are not ready or they are overheating, it's difficult to say. But it was very snappy and oversteery in the lap overall."

articles.title: Muere un piloto de rally y su copiloto sufre lesiones medulares tras un trágico accidente en Mallorca
articles.standfirst: La 550 Challenge Mallorca anunció su suspensión tras el gravísimo incidente acontecido en una de sus especiales
articles.summary: La 550 Challenge Mallorca anunció su suspensión tras el gravísimo incidente acontecido en una de sus especiales
articles.body: El mundo de los rallyes sigue teñido de luto. Tras el gravísimo accidente que originó la suspensión del Rally Villa de Llanes, penúltima cita del SuperCampeonato de España, otro episodio trágico ha marcado a la 550 Challenge Mallorca, cita de las Islas Baleares en la que podían participar vehículos de diferentes clases en el más de medio millar de kilómetros a recorrer en las especiales que conforman la prueba. La competición ha quedado suspendida tras el fallecimiento de un piloto y las gravísimas lesiones de su copiloto después de un incidente. Los competidores se encontraban a los mandos de un Porsche 993 en la especial de Pollença - Lluc cuando llegó el trágico suceso. Fuentes de la Guardia Civil explican que el vehículo cayó por un barranco en la carretera de la Serra de la Tramuntana a la altura de Mortixt. El accidente, con hora marcada sobre la una de la tarde, provocó el fallecimiento del piloto y lesiones medulares de su copiloto, que fue trasladado de inmediato a un centro médico. Acto seguido, la organización de la 550 Challenge Mallorca anunció la suspensión de la prueba. "Es una decisión dolorosa, pero firme e irrevocable, adoptada desde el respeto más profundo y la consideración que merecen unas circunstancias de esta gravedad. En momentos así no existe resultado, clasificación ni objeto deportivo por encima de lo más importante. La competición pasa a segundo plano, y el respeto, la humanidad y solidaridad deben prevalecer", relata su comunicado oficial. La competición balear es una de las diferentes dentro del panorama nacional. En sus 14 tramos y al menos 550 kilómetros de recorrido, los participantes pueden subirse desde a coches de competición, tanto modernos como clásicos, de regularidad y un apartado para coches de serie. En su edición de 2026 se tiñe de luto. "Desde la organización queremos expresar nuestro más profundo pesar y trasladar nuestras más sinceras condolencias a la familia y a los allegados, haciéndoles llegar todo nuestro apoyo y cercanía ante una situación tan difícil", cierra el comunicado de la prueba.

articles.title: Verstappen destroza a todos y Antonelli se diluye
articles.standfirst: Séptimo el líder del Mundial para la parrilla Sprint, donde Alonso saldrá 15º y Sainz 22º
articles.summary: Séptimo el líder del Mundial para la parrilla Sprint, donde Alonso saldrá 15º y Sainz 22º
articles.body: Max Verstappen se ha adjudicado en modo depredador la 'minipole' para salir primero en el sprint del GP de Singapur. El holandés ha destrozado a todos sus rivales y partirá por delante de Russell y Leclerc, pero sobre él pesa una investigación por posible incumplimiento de banderas amarillas. En todo caso, el rey de la F1 actual ha vuelto y tras su victoria en Malasia muestra tener coche para vencer en un circuito en el que nunca ha ganado antes, aunque sea en el sprint del sábado. Russell clavó su intento final para superar a Leclerc y para meter algo de presión a Kimi Antonelli, séptimo y muy apagado, aunque hay que recordar que para el domingo pesa sobre el inglés una sanción por cambio de motor que le manda al fondo de la parrilla. Ha sido una de las peores actuaciones del líder del Mundial, sin medias accidente, y parece que la presión empieza a hacer mella, aunque su ventaja es tan grande, que en modo 'eco' puede seguir como primero hasta el final en diciembre. En en lado de los españoles, Fernando Alonso lo dio todo, pero en Aston y su motor Honda no rindieron como se auguraba en Singapur. Le falta mucho ritmo en comparación con los RB y los Alpine, que parecen en otro planeta para el actual AMR26B. Partirá 15º el asturiano, tras pasar con solvencia a la Q2, pero los puntos (a partir del 8º) parecen muy lejanos para la carrera corta del sábado. Por su parte, Carlos Sainz tuvo un problema en la entrega de potencia y eso le condicionó en la Q1, donde terminó 22º y último. Para él será otra carrera de pruebas y aprendizaje. Ojo, porque parece que el problema de potencia se produjo en varios equipos y se avecina una investigación sobre lo sucedido. Fue una SQ1 donde además se prohibió el modo adelantamiento, por lo que todo es muy raro. El asturiano mejoró por dos veces su mejor tiempos, pero no estuvo cerca de pasar a la Q3, pues le faltó medio segundo respecto a Pierre Gasly, que marcaba el corte como décimo. Partirá 15º en el Sprint. Los Ferrari se perfilaban como favoritos, pero había que cambiar a las gomas blandas de forma obligatoria, En una serie muy extraña, donde el modo adelantamiento no se podía utilizar, Alonso pudo entrar en la Q2 como 14º, mientras Sainz, con problemas terminaba 22º. Otro lío de un sistema que se activa desde fuera. Verstappen era el primero, con Leclerc a 0.018 y Sainz parece que tuvo una salida de pista en la curva 8, cuando estaba en tiempos para entrar en la Q2. Tiempos. cortesía de formula-timer.com.

articles.body: Carrera Sprint en Marina Bay. El Gran Premio de Singapur nos trae más acción a la pista con un sábado bastante movidito: Carrera Sprint y Clasificación. Una 'pole' magistral para Max Verstappen. El neerlandés parecía dormido tras haber quedado 6º en el Libre 1 de por la mañana, hasta que llegó la hora de la verdad. Un 1.31.156 ha sido el tiempo con el que el de Red Bull ha destrozado el crono, llevándose la primera posición para la carrera de mañana. A Max le siguen muy de cerca Russell, quien tiene ganas de reivindicarse tras los múltiple problemas que cada vez le alejan más del Mundial, y Leclerc, quien parece tener algo especial en Marina Bay. El joven líder del Mundial no está brillando como le gustaría. Kimi quedó 7º en el Libre 1 y en la clasificación sprint de por la tarde, a poco más de medio segundo de Verstappen. Aún y así, el italiano siempre puede sorprender y dar un golpe de mesa cuando menos lo esperamos. A pesar de que podría ser un Gran Premio con el que soñar, la realidad vuelve a golpear de forma muy dura a los españoles. Carlos Sainz tuvo bastantes problemas al no poder activar el modo adelantamiento, por lo que el madrileño tendrá que salir último en la Carrera Sprint de mañana. Mientras, Alonso corrió con algo más de suerte, pero no como para tirar cohetes. El asturiano sabe dónde están los límites de su Aston Martin y siempre trata de sobrepasarlos, por lo que mañana saldrá 15º Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Singapur de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. articles.title: La FIA reconoce un "error humano" que afectó a varios coches, entre ellos Carlos Sainz
articles.standfirst: Nuevo escándalo en Singapur tras lo sucedido en Sepang
articles.summary: Nuevo escándalo en Singapur tras lo sucedido en Sepang
articles.body: "Durante la primera fase de la clasificación al sprint, se produjo un error humano en Dirección de Carrera ajeno al problema de cronometraje que también surgió en dicha sesión (SQ1). Este incidente provocó que el modo de adelantamiento (*Overtake Mode*) no estuviera disponible tras el periodo de bandera roja en la SQ1. Al constatarse que el modo de adelantamiento no estaba activo después de la reanudación. Se activó durante 27 segundos antes de volver a desactivarse. La FIA reconoce que este desafortunado error humano afectó al rendimiento de ciertos monoplazas, dependiendo del momento de su vuelta y de su posición en el trazado. La segunda y la tercera fase de la clasificación al sprint no se vieron afectadas". Es el comunicado de la FIA que reconoce un error humano en el que varios coches se vieron perjudicados, entre ellos Carlos Sainz, que se quejaba de falta de potencia en su vuelta. Se avecinan reclamaciones tras una qualy sprint ya terminada y posibles impugnaciones del resultado, que pueden virar todo el fin de semana con consecuencias insospechadas todavía. Sainz explicaba lo sucedido en la vuelta final de la Q1 donde buscaba el pase a la segunda ronda. "En la mitad de la vuelta he tenido un problema de software y me ha faltado tiempo y por el motivo que sea la FIA, como en Malasia, ha decidido tirar por la calle en medio y no les he importado que la mitad de los coches tuvieran más potencia que la otra mitad y no sé por qué el deporte hace cosas distintas dependiendo quién esté fuera en la primera vuelta o en la última", aseguraba Carlos sobre la injusticia de la decisión de seguir como si nada. "Hemos hecho una vuelta con medio segundo menos que el resto del fin de semana y aún así, sin problemas de frenos, nos hubiera costado pasar a la SQ2", reconocía sincero en su caso.

articles.title: Alonso, 15º y jarro de agua fría: "Estar tan atrás es decepcionante"
articles.standfirst: El español creyó que su vuelta valía el pase a la SQ3, pero se encontró con un AMR26 con más problemas de los previstos originalmente
articles.summary: El español creyó que su vuelta valía el pase a la SQ3, pero se encontró con un AMR26 con más problemas de los previstos originalmente
articles.body: La clasificación del sprint del Gran Premio de Singapur devolvió a la tierra a Aston Martin y Fernando Alonso. El español, que venía de su mejor resultado de la temporada (8º) en Malasia y entraba en una pista muy favorable, se encontró con una realidad diferente en Marina Bay. Pasó a la SQ2 y ya es una buena noticia, pero la pelea por los puntos no parece tan cercana pues no pasará de la 15ª posición en la parrilla (11:00 horas, DAZN). Las sensaciones del asturiano se contraponían al tiempo marcado, algo no tan habitual para los pilotos. "He sentido que era una buena vuelta, quizá suficiente para entrar en la SQ3. Pero estar tan atrás es decepcionante, pensé que la calidad de la vuelta era mejor", explicó al finalizar en los medios de la F1. Pudo atacar, pegarse al muro y no encontró el pase al top-10 de la parrilla. El de Aston Martin no pone excusas. Sabe que su coche está cerca de dar el máximo con un paquete que ya han optimizado desde que se presentó en Hungría. "Tenía bastante agarre, el polvo siempre está pero no es un problema. Iba bien, sólo con un poco de subviraje que no resolvimos y debemos mejorar. Pero el coche está en la ventana", recalcó el bicampeón. Eso sí, hay tareas pendientes que pueden afectar a todo el fin de semana en conjunto. Y de los que no se esperaban. "Necesitamos carga aerodinámica y es la gran penalización. Además de más potencia para las rectas", finalizó el de Oviedo. Tendrá que pelear desde atrás y pensar en progresar en una carrera donde suelen aparecer las mejores noticias para el AMR26. Para el segundo Aston Martin, el de Stroll, menos opciones si cabe -18ª posición-. El error humano admitido por la FIA parece que afectó a su coche, pero no existirá una reclamación mayor por su parte. En su análisis posterior, el canadiense prefirió contestar con una frase para todo. "Está bien", lanzó. Su estilo... es el mismo de siempre.

articles.summary: La lucha por la pole y los primeros puntos del fin de semana sobre el asfalto de Mandalika.
articles.body: Después de un viernes dominado por Raúl Fernández en la categoría reina, Izan Guevara en la intermedia y David Almansa en la pequeña, el circuito balinés repartirá las tres posiciones de privilegio y entregará los primeros puntos del fin de semana en MotoGP. Los amantes de las motos tendrán que trasnochar o madrugar mucho para ver las sesiones libres en las tres categorías. La actividad en pista arrancará a las 2:40 h (hora peninsular española) con la segunda sesión libre de Moto3, seguida por la de Moto2 a las 3:25 h. El último entrenamiento libre de MotoGP tomará el relevo a las 4:10 h para dar el cierre a las prácticas del fin de semana. Los primeros en pelear por la parrilla serán los pilotos de MotoGP: la repesca (Q1) arrancará a las 3:50 h en busca de los dos billetes finales para la lucha definitiva de la Q2, programada a las 5:15 h. Una vez conformada la parrilla de la categoría reina, el trazado vivirá un pequeño parón antes de dar paso a las clasificaciones restantes: la de Moto3 se disputará desde las 6:45 h (Q1) y 7:10 h (Q2), mientras que la de Moto2 cerrará el turno clasificador con la Q1 a las 7:40 h y la Q2 a las 8:05 h. El plato fuerte del día llegará a las 9:00 h (hora peninsular española) con la esperada carrera sprint de MotoGP, un vertiginoso asalto programado a 13 vueltas sobre el asfalto de Mandalika. La lucha por la pole y los primeros puntos del fin de semana tendrán lugar este sábado, 10 de octubre, con las sesiones oficiales de clasificación y la posterior carrera corta. articles.title: Singapore GP Sprint Qualifying: Max Verstappen keeps pole position from George Russell after avoiding yellow flags penalty
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen tops Sprint Qualifying and avoids yellow flags penalty after investigation; George Russell second, Kimi Antonelli only seventh; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Fresh from finally winning Red Bull's first race of the season from their first pole last week in Malaysia, Verstappen needed just a single flying lap at the end of SQ3 to claim pole by just over a tenth of a second from Mercedes' George Russell.

But championship leader Kimi Antonelli was only seventh in the other Mercedes, the one featuring their problematic upgrade introduced last week in Malaysia. Russell, who will serve a grid penalty in Sunday's main Grand Prix, is running their older specification car and qualified half a second ahead of Antonelli in the newer one.

Verstappen's pole had appeared had risk for more than two hours after qualifying when he was investigated for passing Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari in SQ1 under yellow flags, which were out for debris on the track after Cadillac's Sergio Perez had hit the barriers.

After speaking to both drivers and analysing telemetry and in-car footage, stewards ruled that while Verstappen had breached the yellow-flag rules by passing Hamilton, they were "satisfied that the overtake was an unfortunate consequence of the significant closing speed differential" given the Red Bull was on a fast lap at the time and so no penalty was applied to the polesitter.

Ferrari had looked to be the team to beat heading into SQ3 and Charles Leclerc held provisional pole after his first lap but the Monegasque was shuffled back to third place in the end.

Hamilton had also looked a pole contender but ended up sixth behind the McLaren duo of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris in fourth and fifth respectively.

Liam Lawson was eighth for Racing Bulls ahead of the Red Bull of Isack Hadjar, who had his SQ3 lap time deleted. Alpine's Pierre Gasly was 10th.

Timing glitch and 'human error' confuse end to SQ1

The start of SQ2 had been delayed due to a timings issue that meant some of the final lap times of SQ1 were not initially registered before a definitive final order was confirmed and qualifying resumed.

The FIA also revealed there had been an unrelated incident due to "human error in Race Control" regarding the activation of Overtake Mode after the debris-triggered red flag in SQ1. It meant drivers experienced different durations of boost mode depending where they were on track during the final laps of the first knockout segment.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz qualified last and felt they had definitely been negatively impacted by the timing of the Overtake Mode being briefly available, while Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad made a surprise early exit in 17th place.

"During the first period of Sprint Qualifying there was a human error in Race Control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1. This issue in question meant Overtake Mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1," read an FIA statement.

"When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of Sprint Qualifying were not affected."

Verstappen said pole was unexpected as Antonelli fears 'difficult weekend' in upgraded Mercedes

Verstappen had topped SQ1 but fell to fifth in the second knockout segment before a single run on the mandatory soft tyres at the end of SQ3 paid dividends.

"It's always close here in Singapore," said the Dutchman, who will be chasing his first grand prix win at the night-time event in 10 attempts on Sunday.

"And also your lap itself, you're pushing as hard as you think is possible, close to the walls in places.

"Once we bolted on the soft tyres, it felt like the car was coming alive a little bit more, but I did not expect this. Of course, [I'm] very happy to be first.

"I think the last few races we have been a lot stronger, but this track still highlights a few little weaknesses in the car, but we manage to drive with them as well as possible."

Russell finished 0.120s behind and was clearly the quicker Mercedes through qualifying despite his W17 being the one without the upgrades introduced at Sepang last week. Mercedes, on the initiation of Russell, are splitting their packages all weekend in a bid to get to the bottom of why the updates have not yet performed as expected.

"We have seemed competitive all day from the first laps in FP1," said Russell.

"We knew Max was fast and he went on a slightly different strategy in SQ3 doing just one lap. Who knows what was best? Pretty satisfied with P2."

But Antonelli, who leads Russell by 84 points in the Drivers' Championship, said he had been "struggling" in his updated W17 from practice onwards.

"Still a lot to understand about this package," said Antonelli. "The car is very difficult, very unpredictable, and very difficult to put a lap together.

"It's a shame because I was coming with high hopes, but so far it's been very difficult."

"I think it's going to be a difficult weekend unless we can pull something out tomorrow."

articles.title: Singapore GP: FIA admits 'human error' created power disparity in Sprint Qualifying at Marina Bay Street Circuit
articles.summary: Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, has revealed a "human error" caused a power disparity in the first part of Sprint Qualifying on Friday; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
articles.body:
Following a red flag for debris in SQ1 caused by Cadillac's Sergio Perez, the FIA did not activate Overtake Mode - an extra power boost that is normally active throughout qualifying and used in races to aid overtaking.

The FIA reactivated Overtake Mode for 27 seconds before deactivating it again, thus causing an unfair advantage in the first part of Sprint Qualifying.

Sky Sports F1 understands the brief re-activation of Overtake Mode happened in the last minute of SQ1 when several drivers were on flying laps before being turned off.

It is also understood Williams petitioned for all teams to progress to SQ2, which was declined, and no protests are expected.

Williams' Carlos Sainz was one of the six drivers to miss out on SQ2 and says the drivers who had Overtake Mode for those 27 seconds gained around half a second.

There was also a timing issue during Sprint Qualifying, which the FIA says was "unrelated" to the "human error".

"This issue in question meant Overtake Mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1," read an FIA statement.

"When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of Sprint Qualifying were not affected."

The human error comes just five days after an "unprecedented" software glitch at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia caused several cars to grind to a crawl or a halt.

Sainz, who qualified last for Saturday's Singapore Sprint at 10am (build-up from 9am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event , claimed half of the field had an advantage in SQ1.

"Half of the cars did their laps with half a second quicker engine than the others," said Sainz.

"There was another software issue with the cars this time around, and we were on the bad end of it.

"For whatever reason the FIA, like in Malaysia, at the end decide to do sporting equity and were happy to do half of the cars in qualy with higher power than the other half of the cars.

"A bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things depending on who is out in Q1 or who is out in lap one."

All of the main contenders progressed to SQ2 although Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll would have fancied their chances of getting through.

Max Verstappen went on to take Sprint pole from Mercedes' George Russell and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Teams keen to understand what happened in SQ1

"Unfortunate human error from the FIA, not the first time we've heard that.

"As far as Aston Martin are confirmed, their sporting director Andy Stephenson is still up with race control. They just want to understand what happened here today.

"They don't believe that anyone was doing their qualifying lap and then didn't have the extra half a megajoule available, what it's concerned about is the tyre preparation on the out-lap.

"Most of the drivers were on the radio saying they didn't have power, so they couldn't do the out-lap they wanted to do. That skews everything else, the rest of the computations they've done.

"While Aston Martin aren't making a protest, they do want to understand what's going on.

"They say the easiest thing would have been to stop the session and do it all again, but you've used your tyres by that time and that's not going to be possible."

articles.title: La FIA indulta a Verstappen y saldrá en la pole del sprint
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés adelantó con bandera amarilla a Hamilton, pero no causará penalización
articles.summary: El neerlandés adelantó con bandera amarilla a Hamilton, pero no causará penalización
articles.body: Respiran aliviados en Red Bull. Max Verstappen no ha sido castigado por la federación internacional y podrá salir primero en el sprint del Gran Premio de Singapur (11:00 horas, DAZN). El neerlandés adelantó con bandera amarilla a Lewis Hamilton en la SQ1, pero tras una larga deliberación no hay castigo al piloto más en forma de la parrilla. Ya firmó la pole y ganó en Malasia, y buscará el doblete en unas calles donde nunca ha vencido. Aunque existió la queja de Hamilton, los comisarios de la FIA han aceptado las explicaciones de Verstappen con los datos de la telemetría y la situación del incidente. Algo lógico. "Estaba acelerando al salir de la curva 7 y al ver la bandera amarilla, levantó. 40 metros antes, Hamilton había levantado y circulaba a menos de 60km/h. El diferencial de velocidad cuando se encontraron era significativo, y Verstappen explicó que adelantó para no frenar con mucha fuerza y crear una situación de inseguridad. Su velocidad era de unos 70km/h menor respecto a otros giros en el mismo lugar", recita el comunicado oficial. "El coche número 3 (el de Verstappen) rompió la regla de banderas amarillas, pero los comisarios admiten que fue una consecuencia de la diferencia de velocidad entre los dos coches y las circunstancias que hacen determinar que no sea penalizado", agregan. Básicamente, pasar era la mejor idea para no pegar un frenazo sorpresivo y era lo más factible ya que Hamilton circulaba a mucha menor velocidad. Así las cosas, la parte alta de la tabla no cambiará. Verstappen saldrá en primera línea con George Russell justo a su lado. Sin duda, un lugar de tensión tras los mensajes habituales que los pilotos se dedican en las últimas campañas. Suelen ser con mensajes punzantes e incluso amenazas como las del final del 2024. El último ocurrió en Austria, con esa pole polémica del británico levantando mínimamente con la bandera amarilla doble tras el choque del neerlandés de Red Bull. "Supongo que habrá que acelerar cuando las saquen", lanzó Max. Ahora su reto es otro, con un Red Bull mucho más rápido y entero en todas las condiciones. "La clasificación seguirá siendo el principal reto para nosotros, aunque creo que la salida... también lo será. Nos toca esperar y ver, daremos lo mejor que tenemos", explicaba el cuatro veces campeón. Su temporada 2026 ha cambiado. El rey ha vuelto y quiere estrenarse en un circuito donde jamás había ganado.

articles.title: Newmarket: Musical Times stays unbeaten with Fillies' Mile victory for Charlie Appleby with William Buick on board
articles.summary: Musical Times confirmed her Classic prospects with a dramatic success in the Group One Fillies' Mile at Newmarket, overcoming a host of traffic problems to land her first success at the top level
articles.body:
Charlie Appleby's youngster had looked a top-class prospect in winning her first two starts on the July Course and at Yarmouth, and completed her hat-trick with facile victory in the May Hill Stakes at Doncaster last month.

Subsequent 1000 Guineas heroine Desert Flower completed the May Hill-Fillies' Mile double two years ago for Appleby and William Buick and Musical Times was the 4/9 favourite to follow suit.

It was not entirely straightforward for odds-on backers, with Buick struggling to find a gap, but once the split did come she quickly went through the gears to beat Aidan O'Brien's Haven by a length.

Appleby said: "I'm delighted and I have to say after two furlongs we just had to hold our breath a little bit and see what was happening, but William was on the class filly in the race and he knew it himself. He was just trying to find those gaps and when he did she quickened up smartly.

"The rest were riding to beat one filly - ours, but credit to her and William they toughed it out and when she found the gaps she did what was needed.

"When she got the run upsides the eventual second she was always going to attack the hill well and the one thing we've seen is she always gallops out strongly.

"She had to work a bit hard there but she will have learned plenty and what I liked about her today was she went to post well and is still learning.

"The fillies division is strong this year and there's some lovely fillies around but they look to be all sprinting fillies while this girl sees out the mile well.

"She was seeing the dip for the first time and probably wanted easier ground and it is nice if they can see the dip.

"But there was no chance of her seeing it when she was rolling down and you could see that rounded action looking a bit enhanced here with the ground being tighter than Doncaster and not being able to see that dip bless her. But I think it's a performance you can mark up a little bit."

Musical Times was made 5/2 from 4/1 with BOYLE Sports for next year's 1000 Guineas and Appleby will take a tried and tested route to the opening fillies' Classic of the year via his usual Craven meeting racecourse gallop.

Appleby added: "There's no doubt about it she needed her class to get her home today but from what we saw I think she is entitled to be one of the favourites for the Guineas. She's done it over the mile and sees it out well.

"We'll put her away now and we'll probably just come here for a racecourse gallop and then on to the Guineas hopefully.

"I would say she is a miler through and through at the minute and she has a lot of natural pace and quickens.

"She could maybe get further and you don't always need to be a proper mile-and-a-half horse at Epsom sometimes and if you are miler who can get a mile and a quarter you might be able to get the job done."

While Appleby holds some reservations about middle-distance possibilities for Musical Times, it is those distances O'Brien feels Haven will thrive over next season after the Dundalk maiden winner took the leap into Group company firmly in her stride when second.

O'Brien said: "She's only a baby, is progressing lovely and I'm delighted with her run.

"We have always thought she was a nice filly and she's going to be lovely next season.

"She's progressing and the other filly is a big mature filly, so we couldn't be happier.

"I think she's probably an Oaks filly, a mile and a quarter and a mile and a half. She's going to be a middle-distance filly."

articles.title: Monte Dutton, remembered as 'joyful soul' with entertaining style of writing, dies at 68
articles.summary: Monte Dutton was a well-known Upstate sports writer who spend decades covering NASCAR and writing books. He has died. He was 68.
articles.body:
Fond memories are being shared about Monte Dutton, award-winning NASCAR writer and Upstate novelist who died Oct. 8, his family confirmed. He was 68.

Dutton was a Clinton native and Furman University graduate. He was a resident of Brevard, North Carolina.

Dutton covered NASCAR for the Spartanburg Herald-Journal and the Gastonia Gazette in the 1990s. He was also editor of FasTrack magazine covering motorsports.

His extensive work on writing about NASCAR for nearly two decades included biographies of drivers Jeff Gordon and Tony Stewart. Dutton wrote nine books in all, including Americana music, of which he considered himself a part of as a song writer and guitar player. In his later days, Dutton wrote about local sports in Laurens County.

Dutton was honored for Best Sports Column in 1994 from the National Newspaper Association. He won five awards each from the National Motorsports Press Association, the Eastern Motorsports Press Association and the South Carolina Press Association.

Here are some of the things being shared on social media:

"Sad to see the news of the death of Monte Dutton. He was a pivotal member of the NASCAR media corps for decades. He for sure could tell and write a story that informed and entertained." − Bob Pockrasss, NASCAR reporter for Fox Sports

"In a media world increasingly filled with blandness, Monte stood out." − Jim Noble, Wofford athletics broadcaster and former NASCAR reporter.

"He was a real character of the media center in NASCAR's golden years," − Aaron Bearden, NASCAR journalist.

"He was an excellent writer and a good musician. He always had a unique way of addressing issues." − Deb Williams, NASCAR journalist.

"Monte Dutton was a critical, detailed observer of racing. His writings captured the action and emotions of our sport. RIP. − Mike Joy, NASCAR broadcaster.

"Monte Dutton was a joyful soul, a friend to many, incredible storyteller, historian, and supporter of Furman Athletics. He lived a fascinating life, and his presence and personality will be deeply missed." − Jason Donnelly, Furman athletics director.

Todd Shanesy covers high school athletics for the Greenville News, Spartanburg Herald-Journal and Anderson Independent Mail in the USA TODAY Network. Contact him by email at todd.shanesy@shj.com . Follow him on X, formerly called Twitter, at @ToddShanesySHJ .

articles.title: Singapore GP: Kimi Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades after disappointing Sprint Qualifying
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli says his upgraded Mercedes is "very unpredictable" after only qualifying seventh for the Singapore GP Sprint; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
After the long-awaited upgrades failed to deliver improved performance when they debuted at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to compare different specifications of the car in Singapore.

Antonelli is running the latest version, which included an additional front wing that had not been available in Malaysia, while George Russell is running the pre-Malaysia version of the car that he won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in last month.

The early evidence was concerning for Mercedes as Russell finished second to Max Verstappen in the shortened qualifying session, with Antonelli more than half a second down on his team-mate in seventh.

Asked whether he was surprised by the performance, Antonelli said: "Yes and no, to be fair. Already in FP1 I was struggling.

"Still a lot to understand about this package. The car is very difficult, very unpredictable, and very difficult to put a lap together.

"It's a shame because I was coming with high hopes, but so far it's been very difficult."

While both Antonelli and Mercedes have built extremely commanding leads in the drivers' and constructors' standings and are near certainties for this year's titles, a lack of clarity in future development direction could have consequences for next season.

"I think it's going to be a difficult weekend unless we can pull something out," Antonelli continued.

"But other than that it's going to be very tricky. I don't really see where we can find seven tenths.

"But you never know. Maybe (Antonelli's engineer) Bono (Peter Bonnington) and the engineers are going to find something in the car.

"And for sure, I'm going to try to improve a little bit the driving, and then we'll see where we'll end up."

Wolff suggests Mercedes may rethink upgrade strategy

Mercedes' major Malaysia upgrade was their first significant new package since May's Canadian Grand Prix and team principal Toto Wolff suggested the Silver Arrows may bring upgrades in smaller steps in the future.

"We felt that the right strategic decision was to work towards a bigger one and then introduce it. Obviously, with the risk of if it doesn't work as you've anticipated, it's just quite difficult to dial yourself out and understand why it hasn't worked," he said.

"So, it's something which we will look at in the future of saying maybe we'll do smaller steps, and then if there is a warning light saying, 'OK', it's easier to undo. But there is no clear way at that stage because so far it has worked.

"I remember 2022. We thought we had one-and-a-half seconds we're putting on the car at the beginning of the season, and that backfired.

"But since then, this year particularly, every upgrade we brought on the car, remember Montreal was a big hit, a big hit in terms of it worked very well. So, if that didn't, why? That's the most important question. And if we come to conclusions that say this is what wasn't as expected, then we have to obviously think for the future."

Russell, who starts on the front row in Saturday's Sprint in Singapore behind pole-sitter Verstappen, says Mercedes will see how Antonelli fares over the remainder of the weekend.

"We can definitely confirm the old one is not bad. Let's see what Saturday brings with Kimi on the upgrade," he said.

"As a team, there's still nothing telling us it isn't working. But it's a sport driven by the stopwatch and the stopwatch has not been great for the upgrade yet. Let's see. Maybe tomorrow (Saturday) is a different day."
